source_notes: Sri Rudra Prashna and Chamaka Prashna from Krishna Yajurveda (Taittiriya Samhita, Kanda 4, Prapathaka 5 and Kanda 4, Prapathaka 7). Source files 'rudra.itx' and 'chamaka.itx' from sanskritdocuments.org, transliterated and proofread by Rajagopal Iyer and Rekha Venkatesh (last updated 2024-08-29 and 2022-03-19 respectively). These are the authoritative svara-marked (sasvaraH) editions from the Vedic tradition. Original encoding: ITRANS with accent marks (\` = anudatta, \' = svarita, \" = deep/dirgha-svarita, {\m+} = long nasal/anusvara). Converted to Unicode Devanagari using: \u0952 (anudatta ◌॒), \u0951 (svarita ◌॑), U+A8F3 (long M ꣳ). Udatta remains unmarked per Krishna Yajurveda convention.

swara_conventions.svarita_falling_tone: ॑ (◌॑) - small vertical line above the syllable
swara_conventions.long_nasal: ꣳ (U+A8F3) - Vedic sign for long nasal 'M' (gM)

extraction_notes.text_variant_details: 9 mantras show minor text differences between our existing rudram_data.json and the sanskritdocuments.org source. These are genuine recension variants or sandhi differences (not errors). Examples: 'अदृश्रन्न' vs 'अदृशन्न' (Nam 1.4), 'गिरिशयाय' vs 'गिरिशाय' (Nam 5.2), 'हृदय्य' vs 'ह्रदय्य' (Nam 9.2), 'दिष्णिया' vs 'धिष्णिया' (Cham 8.1). In these cases, the swara-marked text below preserves the source's reading (including its swaras), which may differ slightly from the consonantal spelling in rudram_data.json.
